C1.worst_defect: Hero lede explains Vendure as 'the open-source headless commerce framework', jargon a shop owner does not use and skips past

C2.worst_defect: Refund row admits 'The refund stays Pending until an administrator settles it with two Admin API calls' but never says who does that or how hard it is for a shop whose store was built by a freelancer
C2.where: home.desktop.02 'Live demo or your own store' table, Refund row

C3.worst_defect: No recommended counter hardware: 'tablets and phones, an iPad included, are not tested yet' and only desktop Chrome is tested, so the owner cannot tell what device to put on the counter for tomorrow's first sale; there is also no single staff-ready 'before you open' checklist

C4.worst_defect: Changelog is written for developers ('order.create v5 custom lines are real order lines on a plugin-owned, disabled ... variant', 'ADR 0005', 'TallyPosV51790900000000'), and Troubleshooting mixes counter-staff steps with tallyResolveNeedsAdmin GraphQL; at-the-till screenshots show 'open since 22:06' next to 'Last synced 10:06 PM'

C5.worst_defect: Cashier-sheet and closure screenshots sit in oversized, heavily padded grey frames that waste space and shrink the content

C6.worst_defect: Phone header shows only Docs and Live demo; 'At the till', the page a cashier needs, and 'Quick start' are hidden behind the chevron menu, and at-the-till runs as one long nine-slice column

C7.worst_defect: Lighthouse flags 'unused-javascript: Est savings of 53 KiB', 130 ms render-blocking and 14 KiB legacy JS (still 98/100/100/100)

overall_worst.defect: The site never tells a shop owner what to run the till on at the counter: 'Its browser tests run in desktop Chrome; tablets and phones, an iPad included, are not tested yet' is the only device guidance, so 'can staff sell tomorrow' ends in a hardware guess
overall_worst.fix: Add a short 'Recommended counter setup' box to At the till and to Before you start: a laptop or desktop with Chrome, a USB keyboard-wedge barcode scanner, any printer the browser can print to, the card terminal standalone, and the drawer opened by hand, plus a five-line 'before your first sale' checklist (sign in, opening float, test scan, test sale, print X report)
